name: Quantity
summary: Makes an amount and its unit one value with arithmetic of its own, so that a number whose meaning depends on a unit cannot be used as though it were a bare number.

roles.name: Quantity
roles.summary: An amount together with the unit that gives it meaning, carrying the arithmetic Fowler draws on it in figure 3.2 — addition, subtraction, scaling, division and comparison. The pattern is the refusal as much as the pairing: adding millilitres to milligrams and comparing a weight to a length must fail, and a model that keeps the unit in a neighbouring field cannot make either fail.

roles.name: Amount
roles.summary: The number. Marked because it is the member a rule must never find alone: every reported unit error begins with something reading this and doing arithmetic on it.

roles.name: Unit
roles.summary: What the amount is measured in. Its presence is what makes the quantity self-describing, and what lets a conversion be asked for rather than assumed.
